data.title: 'Glaciers in Himalayas retreating': Nepal floods triggered by 'glacier collapse & massive landslide'
data.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Joseph Shea, Glaciologist and Associate Professor at the University of Northern BC. Shea argues that the catastrophe should be understood as a compound event in which a glacier failure and a massive landslide occurred together. His analysis places the disaster within the broader, well-established transformation of the Himalayas under climate change. As warming changes high-mountain environments, scientists may increasingly need to identify subtle precursors to rare but potentially devastating cascading hazards.

data.title: The extraordinary untold story of Freddie Mercury: Mary Austin on her best friend – and love of her life
data.description: He was Queen’s flamboyant frontman. She was his shy girlfriend, dreaming of marriage until they both realised he preferred men. Thirty-five years after his death, in the week he would have turned 80, Mary Austin talks about their unbreakable bond There were four silver trunks in Mary Austin’s attic that she packed in the mid-1980s and hadn’t opened since. It was too painful. Almost 40 years on, in 2022, she opened one. It was crammed with lyrics from songs written by Freddie Mercury – Don’t Stop Me Now, Killer Queen, We Are the Champions and, of course, Bohemian Rhapsody. She shut the case. It was still too painful. “To say I was overwhelmed is an understatement,” she says. “I couldn’t look at the lyrics. I felt as I did when I originally packed them – that they were his personal belongings and I was being offered an opportunity to delve into them, and I couldn’t do that.” Eventually she asked her two sons to sift through the treasures on her behalf. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘If you build something vastly smarter than you, it better be on your side’: can we stop AI from deceiving us?
data.description: We are used to the idea that our fellow humans might intentionally mislead or manipulate us, but the idea that machines can now do the same is deeply unsettling. Researchers are racing to find solutions before it’s too late The summer issue of the Long Read magazine is out now. Click here to order In November 2023 – a lifetime ago in the field of artificial intelligence – some of the most powerful people in the world descended on Bletchley Park, the wartime codebreaking hub in Buckinghamshire, to talk about AI safety . In attendance were the then US vice-president, Kamala Harris, the AI bosses Sam Altman and Dario Amodei, delegations from 28 countries, two of the three so-called “godfathers” of AI, and Elon Musk. The first iteration of ChatGPT had been released only a year earlier, and there was already plenty of evidence that AI models could be used for ill, from spreading misinformation to generating deepfakes. A presentation at the summit, however, highlighted a different issue: what if the biggest problem wasn’t to come from people misusing the technology, but from AI’s own behaviour? Continue reading...

data.title: From Bill Gates to Bernie Sanders, most agree the AI arms race is disastrous. Only Europe can make it stop
data.description: An EU export ban on Dutch tech giant ASML’s machines could force the pause we all need At this point, it should be clear that AI is a choose-your-own-adventure book where every option ends in disaster. Exploding carbon emissions and ecological collapse? Turn to page 37. Other outcomes include some or all of: the bubble bursting and an ensuing financial crisis ; mass unemployment via automation; the end of democracy and the rise of authoritarian surveillance states; raving cults who believe the pattern-matching algorithm is a consciousness; terrorists who create devastating bioweapons; nation states that deploy autonomous weapons systems that act on non-human timeframes; nation states or terrorists that hack all the myriad systems we depend on; or an AI that, conscious or not, pursues directives that are at odds with human wellbeing. Imagining that people such as Elon Musk, the OpenAI boss, Sam Altman, Palantir’s Peter Thiel and the Trump administration tech adviser Marc Andreessen will lead us to a utopian future of flourishing environmentalism, social harmony and endless leisure requires hallucination and sycophancy so great that that choose-your-own-adventure scenario could only have been written by ChatGPT. Alexander Hurst writes for Guardian Europe from Paris. His memoir Generation Desperation is out now Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’m not nervous, I’m ready’: Tschabalala Self on racist vandals and her bold striding woman for the Fourth Plinth
data.description: The last time she displayed a sculpture in public in Britain, someone covered it in white paint. But, undeterred, the acclaimed artist is a placing a black woman in Trafalgar Square Tschabalala Self is relentlessly positive and unstoppably optimistic. The US artist is waiting for the unveiling of Lady in Blue, her new sculpture for the fourth plinth in Trafalgar Square, London, a towering, colourful painted bronze of a black woman striding (positively, optimistically) into the future. Self seems resolutely hopeful about the work, which is pretty impressive considering what happened to her last public sculpture in the UK. “Yeah,” she says, speaking from her home in upstate New York. “I mean, that was a completely racist act.” In 2022, Self unveiled Seated at Coal Drops Yard in King’s Cross, London. Like Lady in Blue, it was a vast, brightly painted bronze depiction of a black woman, this time seated demurely on a chair. After being shown at Coal Drops Yard without incident, it was moved to the De La Warr Pavilion in Bexhill-on-Sea, where the reception wasn’t quite as warm. “Within the first week,” says Self, “it was spraypainted white, but only on the skin of the sculpture.” As vandalism goes, it doesn’t get much more pointed, or racist. “The first feeling I had was just pain that my sculpture had been harmed. That someone had enacted violence on an object I had imbued with love and affection.” Continue reading...

data.title: Madrid residents brace for noise and disruption from new F1 circuit
data.description: City council emphasises economic case for Madring amid local outrage over disruption and environmental impact Opponents of Madrid’s newly constructed Formula One circuit have accused the regional authorities of putting profit before people’s wellbeing after tests for the inaugural Spanish Grand Prix at the track later this month yielded noise levels that were many times the legal decibel limit. The regional government of Madrid and the city council are hoping that the 5.4km-long (3.3 miles) Madring circuit – which has been built in the north-east of the Spanish capital at a cost of €83m (£71m) – will attract visitors, boost the local economy and put the city firmly on the motor racing map. The Madring bills itself as “a perfectly connected circuit: just 20 minutes from the city centre”. Continue reading...

data.title: Iceland’s close ties with EU mean no vote is not a Brexit-style rejection
data.description: A yes to membership would have given Brussels a boost but Icelanders have not voted to isolate themselves Iceland’s 52.8% to 47.2% vote against reopening EU accession talks is, undeniably, a blow for Brussels. But claiming it as a Brexit-style victory for “national sovereignty” or evidence of broad rejection of the EU misrepresents the reality of the island’s relationship with the bloc. For the EU, Iceland was a dream candidate: small, stable, prosperous and strategically located in an increasingly contested Arctic. Eager as it is to wield more geopolitical clout and revive flagging momentum around enlargement, a vote in favour would have given Brussels a very welcome boost. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump threatens further action as US and Iran exchange fire in new flare-up
data.description: Washington says it acted after observing Iran was planning to deploy fresh mines in strait of Hormuz The US and Iran have exchanged fire for the first time in a month, with missiles and drones fired at Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the strait of Hormuz, and Iran targeting US military bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates in response. The US president, Donald Trump, on Monday threatened further action. The US is trying to prise open Tehran’s grip on shipping going through the strait, which before the war accounted for a fifth of the world’s seaborne energy supply. Washington claimed that Iranian control over the waterway had been loosened by repeated US attacks on Iranian missile launchers and radars. Continue reading...

data.title: Kākāpō rising: 90 chicks swell population of the world’s heaviest parrot
data.description: Critically endangered New Zealand bird enjoys record breeding season triggered by mass fruiting of native tree, pushing its numbers to 325 The population of the world’s heaviest parrot, the kākāpō , has surpassed 300 birds for the first time in 75 years, after a record breeding season triggered by the mass fruiting of a native New Zealand tree. Ninety chicks were officially added to the population of the critically endangered birds on 1 September, pushing the total to 325 – a record high since recovery efforts began. Continue reading...

data.title: How intense rains in the Grand Canyon turned into a deadly disaster
data.description: Flash flooding in Arizona tourist destination was likely triggered by compounding climate factors, such as drought and warming in Pacific Ocean Remote Grand Canyon lodge hit by deadly flash flood boasts fabled history A deadly flash flood in the Grand Canyon over the weekend was likely driven by a confluence of climate factors, including drought, wildfire scarring and warming temperatures in the Pacific Ocean that can supercharge storms. At least two people have died, nearly 80 people were rescued and one remained unaccounted for after a surge of water and debris swept through the immensely popular tourist destination on Saturday, fueled by torrents of rain that hit the national park’s Bright Angel Creek area. data.title: Life after Maga: the group offering an ‘exit ramp’ for rightwingers questioning Trumpism
data.description: The non-profit Leaving Maga is built on the premise that abandoning the Trump-built movement is like fighting a disease or breaking an addiction Stephania Messina kept birthing boys. In the Quiverfull conservative Christian church she belonged to outside Detroit, Michigan, that made her a community celebrity. Your quiver, as the church taught it, is your womb, meant to be filled with as many arrows – a metaphor for children – as you can shoot unto the Lord. She shot five. “They treated me like I was Mother Mary, like I was this gift to the church,” she said. But while she was quickly pushed into leading worship and Bible study groups for women and children, she wasn’t permitted to talk about politics. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I had no love for myself … now I have peace’: former Ireland rugby player Ryan Caldwell’s journey back from the edge
data.description: The retired second-row on his recovery from addiction, depression and incarceration to find a new life as a meditation teacher “Carefree,” says Ryan Caldwell when I ask him what word is tattooed across his fingers. He looks up from his hands on a rainy morning in Belfast. The former Ireland international, who played the role of enforcer for Ulster, Bath and Exeter, then laughs softly in acknowledgment of that incongruous word. We have spoken for almost two hours about a wide range of dark and heavy subjects – from his addiction issues and imprisonment to his injury-riddled rugby career and the last big concussion that ended his playing days and sent him plunging into a deeper spiral of suicidal depression. data.title: Summer box office 2026: what can we learn from the hits and misses?
data.description: It was a bumper season for Hollywood, almost back to pre-pandemic levels, with Tom Holland blockbusters winning out, but there was still a string of disappointments As the world continued to burn and temperatures reached worrying highs, most of us decided to take refuge in the cinema this summer. It provided some relief for audiences, but even more so for the industry at large, with the season pushing past the magic $4bn mark to become the biggest since 2019, up 20% from last year. There were the expected hits (Spider-Man never misses), but there were also unprecedented breakouts (we were obsessed with Obsession) and surprise underperformers (are kids Minions-ed out?) So at the end of a season with epic highs and cavernous lows, what lessons can Hollywood learn? Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I feel like I’m grieving’: staff on the devastating fallout of widespread layoffs at Xbox
data.description: Last month, Microsoft’s gaming division told its workforce it was cutting 3,200 jobs, which some say will have big ramifications for game development – as well as taking a huge personal toll On the morning of 6 July, an email went out from Asha Sharma, the chief executive of Xbox, to all of the division’s employees around the world. Under the headline “ Resetting Xbox ”, it announced the most significant restructuring in the history of Microsoft’s console business: 3,200 staff would be laid off throughout the financial year to 2027, and 1,600 of those roles would be eliminated immediately. An hour later, at studios throughout company, the Teams meeting invites started arriving. “It was a virtual call with our studio manager,” says Anne Barrett, who was laid off from Bethesda Game Studios Austin. “All of our cameras and microphones were turned off so we weren’t able to say anything or react to anything. We were just brought in, told the news and it was like: ‘You guys are going to lose access to your Slack channel.’ So you saw a flurry of goodbye messages before everything was just shut off.” Continue reading...

data.title: A walking tour of Andalucía’s historic white villages: ‘Nightingales serenade us as we wind along lush river valleys’
data.description: The famous pueblos blancos in southern Spain’s Sierra de Grazalema natural park teem with wildlife amid a limestone wonderland of peaks ‘The wind is in from Africa / Last night I couldn’t sleep.” Joni Mitchell has ear-wormed her way into my head as my wife and I step out from Zahara de la Sierra into the mountains of Sierra de Grazalema natural park. The Africa bit probably comes from yesterday’s visit to Zahara’s castle museum. Here, high above the tiled terracotta mosaic of village rooftops, we learned how the recapture of this picturesque hill town was a turning point in the Reconquista – the military campaign of the 1400s that saw the Catholics retake southern Spain after seven centuries of Moorish control. As for sleep deprivation, I may just have overdone it on last night’s tapas. Either way, Africa feels present as we tramp through the countryside of Andalucía, if only in the wildlife. The painted lady butterflies drifting over the flower-spangled verges, the turtle doves purring from the olive groves and the booted eagle drifting overhead: all are summer visitors recently blown in from the great continent to our south. Continue reading...

data.title: Raygun: Breaking Badly review – the ridiculed Olympic B-girl gets the last laugh … and it’s a total joy
data.description: She spent the biggest moment of her career at the Paris Olympics thrashing around like a toddler having a tantrum – then went viral globally. Now, a new Netflix film reveals how the much-mocked breakdancer got over it Netflix’s Untold is ostensibly a series of sports documentaries. However, since its inception five years ago, it has been most successful when sport collides with the wider celebrity machine. There have been films about Caitlyn Jenner, Jake Paul and Vinnie Jones. The gold tends to come when the subjects spill over into public notoriety. With that in mind, it was only a matter of time before they made a film about Raygun. You may remember Raygun as the Australian breakdancer who spent the biggest moment of her career at the Paris Olympics thrashing around like a toddler having a tantrum in a supermarket. If you didn’t see her routine, you will almost certainly be aware of the memes she inspired. Adele discussed her during a concert. Rachel Dratch did an impersonation of her on Jimmy Fallon. For months, Raygun was everywhere. As this film demonstrates, she really didn’t want to be. Continue reading...

data.title: The Nepal and Tibet flood is a warning: melting snow and ice will bring more disasters around the world |  Bill McGuire
data.description: In Alaska, the Himalayas, the Andes, Greenland, and perhaps also the Alps, deadly chain reactions are just waiting to be triggered You may not have felt it, but the earth beneath our feet is getting twitchier, and global heating is to blame. As temperatures surge and climate breakdown accelerates, interactions between climate and geology are becoming ever more apparent – as marked by last week’s horrific events in Nepal and Tibet . We still have a bit of a blind spot when it comes to the idea that a changing climate can impact what scientists call the geosphere, but the evidence has long been incontestable. In 2021, a similar deluge ripped through a series of mountain valleys in the Indian Himalayan state of Uttarakhand , severely damaging two hydroelectric power plants and taking about 200 lives. In August 2025, a colossal landslide in an Alaskan fjord created a 500-metre-high wave in an area frequented by cruise ships. A few months earlier, the collapse of part of a glacier in Switzerland’s Valais canton caused a debris-laden torrent that destroyed and buried most of the already evacuated village of Blatten. Bill McGuire is professor emeritus of geophysical and climate hazards at UCL. His latest book is The Fate of the World – a History and Future of the Climate Crisis Continue reading...

data.title: Nepal’s glacial collapse foreshadowed a future of climate disaster | Michael Mann
data.description: The deluge capped a summer of extreme climate events, from deadly heatwaves to wildfires. We must take action now For millennia, the high peaks of the Himalayas were held together by an invisible, frozen cement – permafrost and glacial ice that bound ancient rock into seemingly unshakable fortresses. But as the planet continues to warm, this alpine glue is liquefying. The glacial collapse and deluge in Nepal and Tibet was not a freak weather event ; it was the structural failure of a mountain itself, nature’s latest commentary on the deadly consequences of human-caused planetary warming. And it was the exclamation point on a summer of extremes, illustrating with a sole unnatural disaster the apocalyptic future that lies in store if we fail to take dramatic climate action. Continue reading...

data.title: Cities sweltering and the smell of the middle ages: has the climate crisis killed Instagram’s Euro summer? | Brigid Delaney
data.description: Who dreams of having a Euro summer now when staying in an ancient, uncooled building in the Old Town is like trying to sleep in a wood-fired pizza oven? This week the Euro summer comes to an end – and so does a certain type of posting on Instagram. Waiting at the bus stop in the grey winter dawn, a slanting rain soaking your trouser leg, you can warm yourself by scrolling your feed and seeing pictures of Australians enjoying a Euro summer. There it is again – azure Greek coves, plates of barbecued sardines, the yachts rented by the hour, and selfies on the balcony of some Paris Airbnb, drinking wine in the long, blue night. data.title: How misconceptions and woeful PR allowed Musk to shred USAID so easily | Jeremiah A Carew
data.description: A year on from the purge, with thousands of jobs cut and billions in foreign aid lost, a former leader reflects on the sorry saga – and why it would never happen to Nasa A year has passed since I and thousands of colleagues lost our jobs at USAID. Asking myself “Why us?” I have come to the conclusion that the American public had very little idea of what we were doing and why. Doge, the “department of government efficiency” , began its work in January 2025, with USAID as its first target, in a reckless campaign that even Elon Musk has said he would not repeat . At that moment of chaos, Americans lacked the knowledge that could contradict the false narrative presented by Musk , who called the agency a “criminal organisation” and “a viper’s nest of radical left-marxists who hate America”. data.title: The Guardian view on regulating big tech: Meta has got off too lightly | Editorial
data.description: New child safety measures are welcome, but the wider risks posed by these platforms remain unaddressed “Hook, hold, harvest and hide” was how Megan O’Neill, a lawyer for the US state of California, characterised Meta’s business model in the trial that ended last week with an $18bn settlement, to be shared between the states and territories that brought the case. It was a clever way to describe the company’s approach to users’ attention and data. But the sharpness of her words was not matched by the deal. While the strengthening of child safety features is welcome, the tech giant once again batted off efforts to alter its products. Meta’s decision to settle enabled it to avoid any admission of liability. It put a stop to the awkward questions being asked of witnesses including Adam Mosseri , Instagram’s CEO, and the damaging claims made by whistleblowers such as Arturo Béjar . This former Meta safety engineer told the court that his own daughter had been sent unsolicited photos of male genitals on Instagram. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on Trump’s immigration crackdown: who will have fewer rights next? | Editorial
data.description: The president’s deportation machine is creating a class of people inside the US who have fewer protections against the power of the state Is the Trump administration creating a group in the US with fewer protections against executive power owing to their immigration status? Its often openly racist actions suggest so. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) claims to target “ the worst of the worst ” – undocumented migrants who commit violent crimes. Yet the Guardian reported that over half of those arrested in July had no criminal convictions or pending charges. That month, ICE made record arrests and deportations, apprehending 1,500 people and removing 1,100 daily. When campaigning, Donald Trump falsely claimed that Haitians were “ eating the pets ”. In office, his administration moved to end temporary protected status (TPS) for Haitians. In June, the supreme court let the protection expire, leaving about 350,000 people at risk of deportation to a country gripped by violence and instability. The court’s decision means more than 1 million TPS holders from 13 nations previously considered too unsafe to return to are now at risk of deportation. Many have lived and worked legally in the US for years. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: ‘Pain-free’ Alcaraz brushes aside qualifier in US Open return after four months out
data.description: Spaniard beats Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 Alcaraz has not played since April with wrist injury As Carlos Alcaraz edged closer to the conclusion of his first singles set in more than four and a half months, like so many times in his career instinct took over. Up 5-4, 30-15 in set one, Alcaraz swept forward to the net behind a precise wide serve and, when his opponent Roman Safiullin responded with a dipping backhand return directly to his feet, Alcaraz delicately pushed a half-volley over the net for a winner. It was a gorgeous shot, a perfect example of the creativity and feel trademarked by Alcaraz that has been missed throughout his extended injury layoff. That touch of genius was followed, predictably, by a wide smile, a quick hold and a comprehensive victory as the Spaniard returned to competition with a stellar 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 win against Safiullin. data.title: Colin Kaepernick knelt 10 years ago. America responded with a clear warning to Black people | Howard Bryant
data.description: A decade after Kaepernick’s quiet protest shook the NFL, his exile looks less like an aberration than a blueprint for the culture war that followed America likes nice round numbers, perfect for anniversaries and reflections, and it has, suddenly, been 10 years since Colin Kaepernick first protested police killings – more accurately, police killings of Black people that went unpunished either internally or by the courts – by taking a knee during the national anthem for the entirety of the 2016 NFL regular season. He never played in the league again. Ten years covers a lot of ground, especially in these years of American darkness, and many of the important details surrounding Kaepernick, his banishment and significance have disappeared, time replaced by more time and more darkness – time moving faster than ever, at internet speed, where nothing matters, where nothing sticks. We consume by clip, by click, by meme, and knowledge by meme is not knowledge at all. Continue reading...

data.title: Elversberg and ‘miracle village’ prove that Bundesliga fairytales still exist | Andy Brassell
data.description: German football has long insisted there is more to their elite league than a title race. Now they have a story that shows the world that surprise and wonder does live here too Friday night was no first day fun for VfB Stuttgart as they got first-hand proof of what the rest of the Bundesliga feared: that Bayern Munich are perhaps mightier than ever. The curtain-raiser, though, didn’t actually set the tone for the the weekend. German football has long insisted there is more to their elite league than a title race, and now they have a story that shows the world that surprise and wonder does indeed live here too. Bayer Leverkusen arrived into their opening fixture of the campaign thinking their season might contain greater certainty than the last one, a more tranquil voyage after being blown off course by almost €300m of player sales and the ill-fated appointment of Erik ten Hag. Enter SV Elversberg, Bundesliga first-timers and representatives of – a “miracle village” as Bild put it – Spiesen-Elversberg, a town with a population of just over 13,000, situated 15km north-east of Saarbrücken, 30 minutes’ drive from the French border. Continue reading...

data.title: Fiorentina’s Serie A renaissance feels a way off after chastening centenary | Nicky Bandini
data.description: The home game against Frosinone seemed a perfect way to celebrate their landmark. It did not work out that way Fiorentina’s 100th birthday party had been going for four days, starting with a fan procession through the historic centre of Florence on Wednesday night and extending to their home game against Frosinone on Saturday afternoon. The club was founded on 29 August 1926, but a decades-old discrepancy in the reporting of that date has led supporters to celebrate traditionally on the 26th. This time they started a few hours earlier, gathering in their thousands beneath the marble façade of the Basilica of Santa Maria Novella on the evening of 25 August and building to a firework show beside the river Arno at midnight. The club’s president, Giuseppe Commisso, stopped by to give a speech. At least one former player, Borja Valero, was among the crowd. Continue reading...

data.title: Marseille’s squad is being gutted but their manager is staying – for now
data.description: It has been a tough transfer window for Marseille and a 2-0 defeat at Monaco suggests it could be a long season By Get French Football News A humid night in Monaco provided an opportunity to gauge the temperature of the Marseille supporters. Despite the ban on away fans at the Stade Louis II, plenty were in attendance for their 2-0 defeat in the Principality. There were cheers for their new manager, Bruno Génésio, and boos for Geoffrey Kondogbia, but it was the silence for much of the second half that spoke volumes. Génésio, who replaced Habib Beye in the summer, has been appointed to keep a lid on things. The former Lille manager has been part of a larger reshuffle at Marseille, with the president and the sporting director also replaced. The new arrivals have inherited a mess. After making promises to Uefa and the DNCG – French football’s financial watchdog – Marseille were allowed to compete in Europe this season. However, if they fail to reduce their wage bill drastically, they will not be allowed to do so next season. Continue reading...

data.title: Burnham to say he wants to unlock ‘positivity’ in first statement to MPs since becoming PM – UK politics live
data.description: Prime minister will bring upbeat message to adversarial Commons after a summer of policy announcements and improved poll ratings Last week it emerged that John Healey , the chancellor, will not set out how the UK will raise defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030 in the budget in October. Instead, he will set out plans to raise defence spending in the spending review next year. The revelation led to Healey being accused of hypocrisy because he resigned as defence secretary in Keir Starmer’s government after Starmer refused to commit to raising defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030 in the defence investment plan published this summer. Healey’s resignation contributed to Starmer deciding to step down, and Healey returning to government in a more senior role as Andy Burnham’s chancellor. For the first time at the spending review, we will set out a clear path about how we will meet that Nato commitment in 2035, of 3.5% of GDP. And as part of setting out that clear path, we will set that target date for 3%. Continue reading...

data.title: Long-term UK borrowing costs at 28-year high as rising oil prices trigger global bond rout – business live– business live
data.description: Renewed fighting in Middle East weighs on financial markets; Shein shares tumble after Hong Kong stock market debut Adding to pressure on the UK’s new prime minister, activity growth in the manufacturing sector has slowed to the weakest since March, according to a closely-watched monthly survey. In better news, hiring at factories picked up to the fastest pace in more than two years last month. The rate of expansion in the UK manufacturing sector cooled in August, with output and new order growth losing traction. There are still signs for continued optimism, however, as manufacturers reported a positive outlook for the year ahead. Business confidence rose to a six-month high and job creation was the strongest for two years. This suggests that the slowdown was mainly driven by a reduced focus on maintaining precautionary stocks as economic uncertainty eases, especially as domestic and overseas clients continue to show a willingness to spend albeit with a relatively high degree of caution. Although cost and supply chain pressures remain potentially damaging, there was better news on these fronts too. Volatility in energy markets, supply constraints, geopolitical strife and transportation disruptions are all keeping cost rises at elevated levels, but August at least saw purchase price inflation descend from recent peaks to a six-month low. In better news, hiring at factories picked up to the fastest pace in more than two years last month. The rate of expansion in the UK manufacturing sector cooled in August, with output and new order growth losing traction. There are still signs for continued optimism, however, as manufacturers reported a positive outlook for the year ahead. Business confidence rose to a six-month high and job creation was the strongest for two years. This suggests that the slowdown was mainly driven by a reduced focus on maintaining precautionary stocks as economic uncertainty eases, especially as domestic and overseas clients continue to show a willingness to spend albeit with a relatively high degree of caution. Although cost and supply chain pressures remain potentially damaging, there was better news on these fronts too. Volatility in energy markets, supply constraints, geopolitical strife and transportation disruptions are all keeping cost rises at elevated levels, but August at least saw purchase price inflation descend from recent peaks to a six-month low. Supply chain delays were the least marked for six months too, which should provide additional respite to cost pressures barring any further major disruptions. Continue reading...

data.title: The Extractor review – Indonesian hostage-rescue thriller has surprising thread of gentleness at its core
data.description: Iko Uwais directs and acts in the story of a band of elite soldiers who must rescue a group of researchers taken captive in the jungle Can an elite team of soldiers rescue a band of innocent hostages from a bunch of mean old terrorists? Yes, probably, since there are few (if any) action movies in which the hostages are wiped out and the terrorists win. Not to be confused with the Extraction action franchise starring Chris Hemsworth as a mercenary named Tyler, nor with action thriller Escape Plan: The Extractors, starring Dave Bautista as a prison security expert named Trent, this is an Indonesian action thriller in which actor/director Iko Uwais plays a soldier named Timur. The film was actually called Timur originally, but there’s no denying that The Extractor is a more commercial title (unless you are particularly interested in the medieval Mongol khanates ) and will attract more viewers to this tale of hostages, heroes and long-ago childhood friends. In some ways, though, the rebrand is a shame, because the new title suggests the film is more generic than it is. While the basic plot, in which a bunch of researchers are taken hostage in the jungle by an armed group of wrong ’uns, is hardly unique, there are sequences in the film that stand out from the direct-to-video action content mill. In Indonesia, timur means “east”, where the sun rises, and it carries the connotation of hopefulness. That softer feeling in the original title is a key part of the film’s identity, which includes sentimental flashbacks to the childhoods of various characters whose lives have taken tragically different paths. (Can you imagine a world in which a terrorist and a soldier knew each other as children? The Extractor can.) Continue reading...

data.title: Pin de Fartie review – spoonerist remix of Samuel Beckett’s Endgame finds fresh absurdity in Argentina
data.description: Beckett’s masterpiece is given a postmodern cinema slant, with characters in different locations, music and humour in a free and fanciful interpretation Remember remixes? Where you take a song and swap out parts of it with new or pre-existing material, changing it just enough to be still recognisable? Argentinean director Alejo Moguillansky applies this quintessentially postmodern aesthetic to film with a funky cinematic remix, or even series of remixes, of Samuel Beckett’s one-act play Fin de Partie, AKA Endgame. The result feels a little retro and possibly a bit too pleased with its own cleverness, and the spoonerist title is juvenile. But in the end this really achieves something with both the source material and the remix that’s fresh, pleasingly provocative, and at times moving. Beckett’s 1957 absurdist masterwork has just four characters on stage throughout, two of whom do most of the talking: cantankerous blind, disabled Hamm banters with his servant/slave Clov, while Hamm’s parents, Nagg and Nell, live in dustbins upstage and talk rather less. There’s an air of apocalyptic doom, much talk of drugs, food and, above all, time running out. Continue reading...

data.title: Parasomnia review – sleep-schedule horror conjures up a succubus on the loose in waking nightmare
data.description: Debut director James Ross II shows promise in this gore fest, but the fear factor suffers from an overly complex plot Sleep has been part of the horror genre repertoire since The Cabinet of Dr Caligari, and the anxieties around it are spiking as the “ sleep economy ” becomes a thing. This ambitiously structured gore fest about a woman suffering from waking nightmares comes with an all-black cast, but race isn’t a central preoccupation here. Instead, as night terrors burst the banks into reality, debut director James Ross II concentrates on maintaining an appropriately scrambled and claustrophobic experience – perhaps to the detriment of the fear factor. On her 15th birthday, Riley (Jasmine Mathews) is paralysed in a waking/sleep state at her foster home, able to observe but powerless to intervene to stop a care worker going berserk. Since this massacre, Riley keeps a strict sleep protocol as an adult, making sure anyone under the same roof drops off before her, which apparently protects them from the malevolent presence invading her nights. Old foster home pal David (Stephen Barrington) accepts an invitation to the house where Riley’s dad murdered her mum, but gets the willies when a pallid demon begins manifesting in the small hours. It turns out that Riley’s boyfriend, Cam (RJ Brown), has been lax in letting her fall asleep before him – and now her resident succubus is on the loose again. Continue reading...

data.title: Anita Brookner by Hermione Lee review – an enigmatic literary great given her due
data.description: A tireless account shines a light on the Booker-winning author’s mysterious early years and the undeserved criticism that accompanied with her success ‘Dr Weiss, at forty, knew that her life had been ruined by literature.” The first fictional sentence Anita Brookner ever published, aged 53, in A Start in Life, certainly set a tone. If people have heard of Brookner today, Hermione Lee says, they imagine a lonely, cardiganed woman yearning for an absent lover. “This,” says Lee (an emeritus English professor at the University of Oxford), “won’t do.” The cardiganed image confuses the author with her protagonists. Of 24 novels written across 30 years, only the first four – A Start in Life, Providence, Look at Me and Hotel du Lac – are about a single woman pining for love. There is certainly a “Brooknerian” style, characterised by elegance, restraint and melancholia, but her fiction engaged with our emotional lives broadly, examining family, exile, home, trauma, ageing and much more. Continue reading...

data.title: Under Story by Chloe Benjamin review – this time-reversal melodrama is quantum hokum
data.description: A grieving couple who have lost their son find a way to a mirror universe where time runs backwards – but the narrative machinery is shonky and distracting There is something farcical – grotesque, even – about life played in reverse. A child falling into a tree. A sandwich emerging from a mouth, bite by reconstituted bite. A doctor unstitching a wound. The world is strange in any order, but rewind helps us notice – makes the ordinary absurd. Novels that pick a fight with forward momentum tend to harness this absurdity, revel in it. In The Cockroach (2019), Ian McEwan gives us a sneering Brexit fable about political nostalgia. If voters want to turn back the clock, let them. He unleashes “Economic Reversalism”, which sees employees pay for the privilege of work, and every pound sent back to where it came from. In Time’s Arrow (1991), Martin Amis inverts the Holocaust. Just imagine it, he dares us: a network of sanatoriums instead of death camps. A vast machinery of reparation run by benevolent Nazis. How monstrously laughable. Continue reading...

data.title: Caregiver creep: how helping elderly relatives can snowball into a full-time job
data.description: Assisting an ageing loved one can start with small tasks but may lead to full-time caregiving that requires more support Helping an ageing parent or loved one often begins with easy-to-field requests: Pick up a prescription. Drive them to a doctor’s appointment. Grab groceries. However, light tasks – just “helping out” here and there – may eventually snowball into the avalanche of full-time caregiving, a phenomenon becoming known as “caregiver creep”. Like “ caregiver burnout ”, it’s not a formal term, but there is growing awareness about this slow build among healthcare providers and experts. Continue reading...

data.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Jerry, the king of dogs, who taught me how to live
data.description: After a burglary, my parents decided we needed extra security. Jerry was the answer – and this hungry, handsome hound helped us all in countless ways Jerry came into our lives because a burglar had broken in. My mum had woken in the middle of the night to find an intruder in our kitchen. He scarpered, but the psychological damage was done. Two days later, my dad came home with the cutest little rescue puppy, with traces of beagle and labrador in him. He was two months old, had a black, brown and white coat, and big, bashful eyes. We called him Jerry because we had a cat called Tom. “I’m not sure how he’ll protect us,” I said. “He will,” my dad replied. Jerry was very laid-back and Zen. He became part of the family straight away. He also became the therapy dog we hadn’t realised we needed. With two teenagers in the house (me and my older brother) and a hyperactive younger brother, someone was always in a strop and needing to let off steam by taking him out for a walk. Each time, Jerry obliged. I’d bore him with my latest teen-romance trauma; he was a very good listener. Sometimes, he’d have five walks a day, with both of my parents taking their turn. He certainly got his steps in. Continue reading...

data.title: Sea otters returned to Canada after extinction; now they protect kelp but threaten a prized 'local delicacy'
data.description: Sea otters, once nearly extinct due to excessive hunting, have successfully rebounded in British Columbia, playing a crucial role in stabilizing kelp forests by curbing sea urchin overpopulation. However, their increasing numbers have drawn attention to the plight of northern abalone, a critical food source threatened by otter predation. Finding the right balance in conservation strategies is essential to protect both species from growing pressures.

data.title: Nasa scientists grew corn in space and found that microgravity changed root and shoot growth
data.description: NASA's recent experiments indicate that corn seeds struggle with directional growth in microgravity environments. Without Earth's gravitational cues, the roots and shoots exhibit erratic growth patterns. Similarly, other plants like Arabidopsis thaliana face similar challenges in space. To prepare for longer missions, NASA is actively designing systems to counterbalance the absence of gravity, underscoring the importance of understanding plant behavior for future food cultivation in space.

data.title: Cientistas usam 'impressão digital' da água para mapear alterações nas chuvas da amazônia

data.title: Em defesa dos studios
data.description: Os studios, ou apartamentos compactos, não são novos no mercado imobiliário . Como relata Raul Lores no livro " São Paulo nas Alturas", a tipologia cresceu nos anos 1940, e, entre 1951 e 1952, o Banco Nacional Imobiliário lançou mais de 1.500 "quitinetes" na capital paulista. Em 1954, o edifício Montreal, de Oscar Niemeyer , tornou-se o primeiro arranha-céu de quitinetes em São Paulo, com apartamentos a partir de 29 m². Leia mais (08/31/2026 - 20h02)

data.title: Fuskanklagade professorn – så splittrar hans död Storbritannien
data.description: Han var stjärnakademikern som blev känd långt utanför forskningsvärlden. Jason Arday växte upp utan att varken kunna tala eller läsa, men blev den yngsta svarta professorn någonsin på prestigeuniversitetet Cambridge. Sedan kom granskningarna av hans forskning, och en lika explosiv som massiv mediabevakning. Debatten går nu hög i Storbritannien – vems fel var det att Jason Arday dog? Programledare: Måns Mosesson. Med Simon Campanello, vetenskapsreporter på DN. Producent: Maria Hansson Botin.

data.title: Bogusław Chrabota: W sprawie Collegium Humanum trzeba mocno przyspieszyć
data.description: Sprawa Collegium Humanum to nie tylko piramidalna kompromitacja systemu edukacji w Polsce. To również mętna woda, w której od lat topione są – sprawiedliwie bądź nie – dziesiątki osób publicznych. Uważam, że kwestią honoru państwa polskiego jest szybkie skierowanie do sądu kompletu spraw związanych z kupowaniem dyplomów. Sprawiedliwe osądzenie i ostateczne wyjaśnienie, kto w tej sprawie zawinił, a kto tylko dostał rykoszetem.

data.description: Vládní hnutí SPD nespáchalo kontroverzními předvolebními plakáty podněcování k nenávisti ani žádný jiný trestný čin. Dnes o tom pravomocně rozhodl pražský městský soud, který vyhověl odvolání SPD a zrušil původní rozsudek. „Jsem rád, že pravomocný rozsudek soudu ve věci našich pravdivých předvolebních plakátů respektuje právo na svobodu projevu,“ sdělil Okamura pro iDNES.cz.

data.title: Rusko pohrozilo devastující odezvou na „protiruské“ činy v Pobaltí
data.description: Mluvčí ruského ministerstva zahraničí Marija Zacharovová pohrozila devastující odezvou na to, co nazvala protiruskými činy v Pobaltí. Hovořila o riziku dalšího nárůstu napětí v regionu. Pobaltské státy jsou členy Severoatlantické aliance, podporují Ukrajinu v její obraně proti ruské invazi a ostře vystupují proti počínání Moskvy.

data.title: Exhejtman Šulc do vězení nemusí. Soud mu zmírnil trest v dotační kauze
data.description: Odvolací soud uložil bývalému hejtmanovi Ústeckého kraje Jiřímu Šulcovi za zneužití pravomoci v rozsáhlé kauze Regionálního operačního programu (ROP) Severozápad tříletý podmíněný trest s pětiletou zkušební dobou. Zmírnil tak prvoinstanční verdikt, podle kterého měl jít na čtyři roky do vězení. Rozhodnutí je pravomocné.

data.title: Pražské Jezulátko zamířilo do Irska. Má vyprávět příběh české metropole
data.description: Kopie sošky Pražského Jezulátka poputuje jako dar do diecéze v irském hrabství Kerry. „Vyjadřuje přátelské vztahy hlavního města Prahy vůči Irsku,“ řekl primátor hlavního města Prahy Bohuslav Svoboda. data.title: Řidič šněroval se škodovkou po silnici na Olomoucku, nadýchal přes čtyři promile
data.description: S těžko uvěřitelnými čtyřmi promile alkoholu v dechu sedl za volant padesátiletý řidič. Jeho putování po silnicích na Olomoucku ale nemělo dlouhého trvání, neboť si policejní hlídka všimla šoférovy nekoordinované jízdy. Policisté pak následnou lustrací zjistili, že muž má platný zákaz řízení všech motorových vozidel.

data.title: Začal nový školní rok. Do lavic usedlo asi 115 tisíc prvňáků
data.description: Dětem v základních a středních školách začal po dvouměsíčních prázdninách nový školní rok. Do lavic v něm podle odhadů ministerstva školství poprvé usedlo asi 115 tisíc prvňáků. Dětí v základních školách podle odhadu úřadu oproti minulému roku ubude, přesto bych jich nadále mělo být více než milion. Na středních školách a konzervatořích by mělo žáků v denní formě studia přibýt.

data.title: Zákulisí gigantického paktu. Trump se ve Venezuele spřáhl s ropným místokrálem
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump slíbil Venezuele demokracii výměnou za odstranění diktátora. Devět měsíců po jeho únosu ale místo populární opoziční lídryně María Coriny Machadové vede jednání téměř neznámá Dinorah Figuerová. data.title: Němci vyrazili do boje s kriminalitou. Na nádražích začal platit zákaz alkoholu
data.description: Na čtyřech německých nádražích v úterý začal platit zákaz konzumace alkoholu. Do poloviny října chce železniční společnost Deutsche Bahn zákaz zavést na všech 5400 nádražích v Německu, které spravuje. Chce tím mimo jiné zlepšit boj proti kriminalitě a vandalismu. Zákaz platí na berlínském hlavním nádraží a nádraží Gesundbrunnen a na nádražích v severoněmeckých městech Kiel a Braunschweig.

data.title: Shein při vstupu na burzu propadl. Investoři pochybují o perspektivě firmy
data.description: Akcie čínského fast-fashion gigantu Shein při debutu na hongkongské burze výrazně oslabily. V úvodu obchodování ztrácely až deset procent a firma tak vstoupila na trh s hodnotou kolem 26 miliard dolarů. To je jen zlomek částky, na kterou ji analytici oceňovali před několika lety. Investoři se obávají zpomalujícího růstu, vyšších nákladů i stále přísnější regulace levného přeshraničního e-commerce.

data.description: Policisté kvůli probíhajícímu trestnímu řízení žádají rodiče dětí, které využívaly služeb relaxačního a masážního salonu Well-Sense v Jablonci nad Nisou, aby se jim ozvali. data.title: Motoristům se nelíbí schodek rozpočtu, budou jednat s Babišem, řekl Macinka
data.description: Vládním Motoristům se nelíbí navržený schodek státního rozpočtu na příští rok, ve čtvrtek o tom budou jednat s premiérem Andrejem Babišem (ANO), řekl v úterý ráno předseda Motoristů a ministr zahraničí Petr Macinka před odletem na Slovensko na schůzku ministrů zahraničních věcí zemí visegrádské čtyřky. Macinka věří, že schodek bude nakonec nižší než navržených 389 miliard korun.

data.title: Pavel v Brodku u Konice zahájil školní rok, při focení s prvňáčky zavtipkoval
data.description: Za potlesku místních dorazil ráno do Brodku u Konice prezident republiky Petr Pavel. V obci na Prostějovsku vítá do nového školního roku žáky prvních tříd. Do obce ho pozvali čtvrťáci ručně psaným dopisem, hlavu státu přivítala dechovka a asi 300 lidí. Zdejší škola zároveň slaví stoleté výročí založení. Pavel se dnes také setká se starosty obcí mikroregionu Konicko.

data.title: Jednání V4 s Japonskem i unijní zasedání. Macinka odlétá na Slovensko a do Irska

V úterý se ve slovenském Tomášově zúčastní společného jednání šéfů diplomacií Visegrádské čtyřky s japonským ministrem zahraničí Tošimicu Motegim. data.title: Kyjev byl v noci pod palbou. Ukrajina zasáhla ruský přístav u estonských hranic
data.description: Při ruských leteckých útocích na ukrajinské hlavní město Kyjev a sousední oblast v noci na úterý zemřelo sedm lidí a více než deset dalších bylo zraněno. data.title: Textil se povinně třídí rok a půl. Obcím náklady vzrostly i několikanásobně
data.description: Více než rok a půl po zavedení povinného odděleného sběru textilního odpadu obce upozorňují na rostoucí náklady spojené s jeho zajištěním. Ceny služeb v některých případech několikanásobně vzrostly. Firmy poukazují na klesající odbyt použitého textilu i zhoršující se kvalitu sbíraného materiálu. Systém, který by obcím mohl finančně ulevit, v Česku stále chybí.

data.title: Zemřel bývalý francouzský premiér Édouard Balladur, bylo mu 97 let
data.description: Ve věku 97 let zemřel bývalý francouzský premiér Édouard Balladur, dlouholetý politický souputník a přítel exprezidenta Jacquese Chiraca. data.title: ‘Massive’ Russian missile, drone attack on Kyiv kills 8
data.description:
KYIV: A “massive” Russian attack killed at least eight people in Kyiv overnight, including seven at a railways depot, officials said Tuesday, as Moscow pressed its air campaign on the Ukrainian capital and surrounding areas.
	The strikes came as children were set to return to school after summer holidays and as authorities tightened security measures following weeks of intensified Russian attacks on the capital.

data.title: World leaders need to see rising oceans in Pacific: UN official
data.description:
KOROR: Leaders from the world's top economies should stand on a Pacific atoll to see the reality of record sea level rise, a top UN official said in Palau on Monday.

	Noting last week's deadly floods in Nepal, United Nations Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed said rising seas in the Pacific were the "other side of that story".

	"We do already know that a warming climate is changing the world's ice at extraordinary speeds, not only threatening the communities below glaciers but adding more water to our oceans," she told reporters.

data.title: Iran president says Tehran would ‘immediately’ reciprocate if US returns to June deal
data.description:
Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tuesday that Tehran would "immediately" reciprocate if the United States returned to a June deal aimed at ending their war.
	"I state explicitly that if the United States returns to its commitments under the aforementioned memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately take reciprocal action," Pezeshkian said at a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan, according to the website of the Iranian presidency.

data.title: California lawmakers pass bill allowing people to identify their Jewish ancestry on state forms
data.description:
SACRAMENTO, California: California would allow Jews to voluntarily identify their Jewish heritage on state forms under a bill the state Legislature passed Monday.
	The bill, which lawmakers sent to Gov. Gavin Newsom’s desk, would require state agencies that collect demographic information to add “Jewish” as an option for ethnicity or ancestry. The goal is to give state officials and researchers better data on Jewish Californians, including their unemployment rates and representation in schools.

data.title: Nepal says death toll rises to 987, bringing total killed past 1,000
data.description:
KATMANDU, Nepal: Devastating floods on the China-Nepal border have killed at least 987 people in Nepal, the disaster authority said Tuesday, taking overall deaths to more than 1,000.

	Chinese state media earlier confirmed 16 people were killed in Tibet, bringing the total toll from Wednesday’s disaster to 1,003.

	The number of missing in Nepal dropped to 3,916, as rescue efforts entered a seventh day, and the bodies recovered rose.

	In China, state media say there 546 people missing, taking the overall number of missing to 4,462.

data.title: Lebanon urges Greece to help implement deal with Israel
data.description:
ATHENS: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun asked Greece on Monday for support in implementing a US-sponsored agreement with Israel, hours after Greece and Israel announced a multibillion-dollar arms deal.

	Israel and Lebanon launched direct talks aimed at ending hostilities after Iran-backed Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war in March by attacking Israel, which responded with massive strikes and a ground invasion.

data.title: 10 Syria security personnel wounded in clashes in Sweida: state TV
data.description:
DAMASCUS: Clashes with local armed groups in Syria’s Druze-majority province of Sweida left 10 government security personnel wounded, state media reported Tuesday.
	The unrest, which took place on Monday, came after two civilians were killed in similar clashes west of Sweida city, according to two local security sources.
	Syrian state television, citing the Internal Security Command in Sweida province, said the number of wounded personnel had risen to 10 after “outlaw groups” targeted points in the Tal Hadid area and the Walgha axis.

data.title: Former gang member found guilty of murdering Tupac Shakur
data.description:
LAS VEGAS: Duane “Keffe D” Davis, a former Los Angeles gang member, was found guilty on Monday by a Las Vegas court of the 1996 murder of chart-topping rapper Tupac Shakur.
	Thirty years after the rap legend’s death, the jury found Davis, 63, guilty of murder after just a few hours of deliberation.
	“Count one, murder with use of a deadly weapon, guilty of first-degree murder with use of a deadly weapon,” the foreperson of the jury announced to the court.

data.title: Woman stabs 2 people in New York City’s Times Square, killing 1, then is killed by police
data.description:
A woman randomly stabbed two people in New York City’s Times Square on Monday, killing one woman, and then was fatally shot by police, according to officials.
	The shooting happened just before 4:30 p.m. next to a New York Police Department substation, just outside One Times Square, the building that hosts the city’s annual New Year’s Eve ball drop celebration. It is one of the most heavily touristed and policed spots in all of New York.

data.title: The 3 biggest chucks on Supplementary Budget are Fuel assistance, El Nino and Debt interest

data.title: Cameroun : le lieutenant-colonel Cerlin Belinga nommé vice-président du tribunal militaire de Maroua
data.description: © DR Par décret présidentiel du 31 août 2026, l'ancien commissaire du gouvernement près le tribunal militaire de Yaoundé cumule avec les fonctions de juge d'instruction près la même juridiction. D’autres personnalités ont été nommées à d’autres tribunaux militaires du pays. Le tribunal militaire de Yaoundé a un nouveau commissaire de gouvernement. Le lieutenant-colonel Éric Atemengue Omgba remplace le lieutenant-colonel Cerlin Belinga nommé vice-président du tribunal militaire de Maroua et juge d'instruction près ledit tribunal. Dans l'exercice de ses fonctions, le nouveau commissaire du gouvernement sera assisté du lieutenant-colonel Brice Josué Onana, nomme substitut du commissaire du gouvernement au tribunal militaire de Yaoundé. Après avoir officié au sein de la juridiction pour veiller à l'application de la loi dans l'affaire liée à l'assassinat du chef de chaîne de radio Amplitude FM Martinez Zogo à Yaoundé, Cerlin Belinga s'en va poursuivre sa mission dans la région de l'Extrême-Nord. Faut-il trouver cette affectation comme une sanction ? À priori, le changement de juridiction et de ville expliquerait une certaine sanction dont le motif reste dissimulé au sein de l'administration de la justice. Cependant, il est plus évident de noter que le décret présidentiel du 31 août 2026 accroît plutôt les responsabilités et les pouvoirs de l'ancien commissaire du gouvernement. Il est en même temps la deuxième personnalité du tribunal et juge d'instruction. Il quitte le tribunal militaire de Yaoundé au moment où le procès de l'assassinat de Martinez Zogo se trouve à l'étape de l'audition des témoins. Son successeur, après avoir pris connaissance des dossiers en cours de traitement, conduira la mission, sans doute jusqu'au dénouement des affaires concernées. Le décret présidentiel de lundi dernier marque un nouveau changement au sein de la juridiction. Depuis le déclenchement de l'affaire Martinez Zogo, des personnes se succèdent à certains postes. À la présidence du tribunal, Jacques Baudouin Misse Njonè a été nommé alors que le procès est en cours. Ce dernier a dessaisi Florent Aimé Sikati Kamwo du dossier d'instruction en décembre 2023 pour le confier à Pierrot Narcisse Nzié. À chaque fois, le tribunal a continué d'assurer sa mission. Ce sera le cas avec l'arrivée du nouveau commissaire du gouvernement. Le décret du président de la République nomme d'autres officiers magistrats au sein des tribunaux militaires. Au tribunal militaire de Bamenda, le chef de bataillon Mokete Roland Makamba est nommé juge d'instruction. Au tribunal militaire de Bertoua, le chef d'Escadron Yaya Hassan est nommé vice-président et juge d'instruction. Le chef d'Escadron Mukum Tifuh Immaculate est le nouveau commissaire du gouvernement près le tribunal militaire d'Evolowa, tandis que le lieutenant Sadam Hamadou est nommé substitut du commissaire du gouvernement au tribunal militaire de Garoua. Cet article Cameroun : le lieutenant-colonel Cerlin Belinga nommé vice-président du tribunal militaire de Maroua est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Faut-il trouver cette affectation comme une sanction ? À priori, le changement de juridiction et de ville expliquerait une certaine sanction dont le motif reste dissimulé au sein de l'administration de la justice. Cependant, il est plus évident de noter que le décret présidentiel du 31 août 2026 accroît plutôt les responsabilités et les pouvoirs de l'ancien commissaire du gouvernement. Il est en même temps la deuxième personnalité du tribunal et juge d'instruction. Il quitte le tribunal militaire de Yaoundé au moment où le procès de l'assassinat de Martinez Zogo se trouve à l'étape de l'audition des témoins. Son successeur, après avoir pris connaissance des dossiers en cours de traitement, conduira la mission, sans doute jusqu'au dénouement des affaires concernées. Le décret présidentiel de lundi dernier marque un nouveau changement au sein de la juridiction. Depuis le déclenchement de l'affaire Martinez Zogo, des personnes se succèdent à certains postes. À la présidence du tribunal, Jacques Baudouin Misse Njonè a été nommé alors que le procès est en cours. Ce dernier a dessaisi Florent Aimé Sikati Kamwo du dossier d'instruction en décembre 2023 pour le confier à Pierrot Narcisse Nzié. À chaque fois, le tribunal a continué d'assurer sa mission. Ce sera le cas avec l'arrivée du nouveau commissaire du gouvernement. Le décret du président de la République nomme d'autres officiers magistrats au sein des tribunaux militaires. Au tribunal militaire de Bamenda, le chef de bataillon Mokete Roland Makamba est nommé juge d'instruction. Au tribunal militaire de Bertoua, le chef d'Escadron Yaya Hassan est nommé vice-président et juge d'instruction. Le chef d'Escadron Mukum Tifuh Immaculate est le nouveau commissaire du gouvernement près le tribunal militaire d'Evolowa, tandis que le lieutenant Sadam Hamadou est nommé substitut du commissaire du gouvernement au tribunal militaire de Garoua. Cet article Cameroun : le lieutenant-colonel Cerlin Belinga nommé vice-président du tribunal militaire de Maroua est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Marché des titres publics Cemac : le Cameroun peine à séduire les SVT
data.description: © DR juillet 2026, le taux de participation des Spécialistes en Valeurs du Trésor aux BTA du Cameroun est tombé à 18,98% contre 20,1% de moyenne Cemac, son plus bas depuis 2023. Le pays affiche 22 SVT agréés mais ne sert que 6,97% d’intérêt, contre 7,87% en Guinée équatoriale et 7,24% au Congo. Alerte sur l’attractivité du Cameroun sur le marché des titres publics de la Cemac. Selon la BEAC, en juillet 2026, le taux de participation des SVT aux Bons du Trésor Assimilables du Cameroun est ressorti à 18,98%, en dessous de la moyenne générale de 20,1%. C’est une première depuis 2023. À titre de comparaison, cet indicateur était de 23,8% en juillet 2023, 26,3% en juillet 2024 et 23,3% en juillet 2025. Conséquence, le Cameroun devient le 2e pays le moins attractif de la communauté pour les BTA, juste devant le Gabon à 16,2%, malgré le plus grand réseau avec 22 SVT agréés. Loin devant, la Guinée équatoriale culmine à 41,6%, suivie de la RCA à 25% et du Congo à 23,3%. La BEAC ne commente pas ce repli, mais le différentiel de taux est éloquent. En juillet, le Cameroun a servi 6,97% sur ses BTA, contre 7,87% pour la Guinée équatoriale et 7,24% pour le Congo. Un décrochage qui s’inscrit dans un tassement global du marché, dont le taux moyen de participation est passé de 26,3% en juillet 2025 à 20,1% en juillet 2026. Cet article Marché des titres publics Cemac : le Cameroun peine à séduire les SVT est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : le MRC dénonce l’interruption brutale d’une réunion privée de ses militants à Bertoua
data.description: © (DR) L’Assemblée des structures du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun de la région de l'Est se tenant dans un domicile privé d'après le parti, a été interrompue sur ordre du sous-préfet de Bertoua 2e, Orfeo Benasconi Nkomo Mimbo'o. 24 heures après l'interruption de la réunion des militants de la fédération régionale du MRC de l'Est, le parti fait le point de la situation en dénonçant les manœuvres du « régime Biya-RDPC ». Le parti d'opposition s'insurge contre la dispersion brutale d'une réunion de ses militants dans un domicile privé dans une barrière par une dizaine de gendarmes. Au cours de cette interruption, les forces de maintien de l'ordre ont interpellé le secrétaire de la fédération régionale et le secrétaire de la fédération départementale du Lom et Djerem. « Embarqués de force sans mandat, sans procédure, sans état d'urgence. Ils ont été placés sous garant et remis en liberté » pour "Réunion publique non déclarée. Les faits remontent au dimanche 30 août 2026. Pourtant, rétorque le MRC, une réunion publique se tient dans un lieu public ou bien ouvert au public. De ce fait, il dénonce un « acte de barbarie d'Etat commandité par le pouvoir en place » et lie cette intervention à une série d'autres actes commis dans le cadre d'une "escalade orchestrée". En font partie, le rejet de la candidature de Maurice Kamto à la présidentielle de 2025, l'interdiction de la première convention nationale extraordinaire du MRC en novembre 2025, la transmission au parti le 20 août d'une lettre datée du 19 août 2026 du ministère de l'Administration territoriale. Lettre notifiant au MRC le refus du ministre de prendre acte des résolutions de la convention de décembre 2025. Face à ces actes, le MRC dénonce aussi la complicité de la justice qui se range du côté du Rdpc en bloquant les plaintes du MRC. La formation politique pointe du doigt des magistrats qui regardent « des extrémistes du pouvoir » matraquer des militants, violer la loi "sans broncher", "sans lever le petit doigt". Dans une communication signée de son secrétaire général adjoint n°1, Roger Justin Noah, le MRC encourage ses militants à rester mobilisés. Au-delà de cette sortie ce lundi, le MRC et le ministère de l'Administration territoriale sont en opposition sur la convention extraordinaire du 21 décembre 2026 tenue en visioconférence. Le ministre Paul Atanga Nji refuse de prendre acte des résolutions de la convention au motif que la convention n'a pas été déclarée au préalable auprès des autorités administratives. Dans une lettre en réponse, le parti conteste les termes du ministre et lui demande quelle autorité administrative est compétente pour recevoir la déclaration d'une réunion qui se tient en visioconférence. Dénonçant la violation de la loi, la formation politique rappelle que d'après la loi, la tutelle n'intervient pas dans le fonctionnement des partis politiques. Aussi le parti exhorte-t-il le ministre à faire une bonne application de la loi no 90/056 du 19 décembre 1990. Le bras de fer qui s'est ouvert pourrait se poursuivre jusqu'à ce que la justice tranche. Cet article Cameroun : le MRC dénonce l’interruption brutale d’une réunion privée de ses militants à Bertoua est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Lutte contre la contrebande : coup de filet à Ebolowa avant la campagne nationale
data.description: © DR 69 cartons de vin rouge Perlado saisis dans la nuit de vendredi 28 août 2026 à Ebolowa par la Brigade Mobile des Douanes, à J-3 du lancement de la campagne nationale de sensibilisation prévue les 31 août et 1er septembre 2026 dans le Secteur Douanes Sud I. La Douane serre la vis. Dans la nuit de vendredi 28 août 2026, les éléments de la Brigade Mobile d’Ebolowa ont intercepté un véhicule de tourisme en provenance de Kyé-Ossi, ville frontalière réputée plaque tournante des trafics. À l’intérieur, 69 cartons de vin rouge de marque Perlado minutieusement dissimulés dans la malle arrière et sous les sièges. Une marchandise de contrebande, sans vignette douanière. Au-delà de la saisie, l’opération relance le débat sur ce macaron fiscal obligatoire. Loin d’une formalité, il est la carte d’identité du produit : il atteste du circuit légal, du contrôle sanitaire et du paiement des droits. Sans lui, le consommateur s’expose à des boissons potentiellement frelatées, tandis que l’État perd des recettes et que les distributeurs légaux subissent une concurrence déloyale. Le timing est fort : l’interception intervient à 72 heures du lancement de la campagne nationale sur les produits sensibles bières, vins, spiritueux, champagne, jus – prévue à Ebolowa et Kyé-Ossi. Objectif : rappeler aux opérateurs l’obligation de vignette et les sanctions, et inviter les consommateurs à vérifier le macaron avant tout achat. Cet article Lutte contre la contrebande : coup de filet à Ebolowa avant la campagne nationale est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: CEEAC : la jeunesse le bouclier de l’Afrique centrale
data.description: © DR À Gitega ce 27 août 2026, le Président de la Commission de la CEEAC, l’Ambassadeur Ézéchiel Nibigira, a appelé la jeunesse africaine à devenir actrice de la paix et de la sécurité, lors d'une Conférence Scientifique. Gitega vibre au rythme de la jeunesse. À l’occasion de la 10e édition de la Journée de la Jeunesse Imbonerakure, la CEEAC a placé les jeunes au cœur du projet d’émergence. Paneliste à la Conférence Scientifique sur la Paix et la Sécurité organisée le 27 août 2026 le Président de la Commission de la CEEAC, Dr Ézéchiel Nibigira, a lancé un appel fort : « La jeunesse n’est pas seulement l’avenir. Elle est le présent, le bouclier de notre stabilité et le moteur de notre émergence collective ». Thème de l’édition : « Innover et Agir : La Jeunesse, Bouclier de la Stabilité politico-sécuritaire, Architecte et pilier de l’émergence du Burundi et de l’Afrique». À ses côtés, le Commissaire Paix et Sécurité, le Général Marcel Mapanou Moussadji, a insisté sur l’engagement citoyen : refuser la désinformation, participer aux systèmes d’alerte précoce et à la solidarité régionale. Des travaux honorés par la présence du Président burundais Évariste Ndayishimiye, Président en exercice de l’UA et Champion de l’Agenda Jeunesse, Paix et Sécurité. Cet article CEEAC : la jeunesse le bouclier de l’Afrique centrale est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : le Nyong et So’o tient des assises stratégiques pour polir l’environnement éducatif
data.description: © DR Du 1 er au 02 septembre 2026, des assises de l'éducation se tiennent dans le département du Nyong-et-So'o sous la supervision du préfet Gille Christian Sadi. Les travaux visent à mettre fin aux dérives en milieu scolaire. La ville de Mbalmayo servira de cadre les 1er et 02 septembre prochains aux assises de l'éducation du département du Nyong-et-So’o. A travers cet événement, les organisateurs veulent s'attaquer à la racine des violences physiques et psychologiques, du harcèlement, des abus sexuels, de la dépravation des mœurs, de la crise des repères civiques, de la prolifération de la drogue et des substances psychotropes, de l’affaiblissement de l'autorité parentale ainsi que de la rupture du dialogue entre les enseignants et les familles. Les travaux se dérouleront à l'auditorium de l’École nationale des eaux et forêts (ENEF) de Mbalmayo sous le thème « Ensemble, faisons de l'éducation le moteur du développement ». Les assises vont réunir des spécialistes de l'éducation, des enseignants, les autorités administratives, les services déconcentrés de l'Etat, les collectivités territoriales, les promoteurs et responsables d'établissements scolaires, des conseillers d'orientation, la société civile, des élèves, les associations de parents d'élèves. Sans oublier les services de santé sociaux, les forces de maintien de l'ordre, les autorités judiciaires les chefs traditionnels, les leaders religieux et communautaires. Les quatre enjeux qui constituent les piliers des travaux sont la protection de l'intégrité physique et psychologique des élèves ; la restauration des valeurs et des repères ; la préservation de la santé et de l'avenir de la jeunesse face aux produits psychotropes ; la mobilisation des parents dans leur rôle de premier éducateur. La rencontre a pour objectif de contribuer à l'amélioration durable du système éducatif local à travers une mobilisation collective en faveur d'une école sûre, saine, inclusive et performante. Il sera ainsi question d'identifier les facteurs qui fragilisent la performance scolaire et renforcer sans relâche la prévention et la lutte contre les violences en milieu scolaire ; promouvoir les valeurs civiques et citoyennes auprès des jeunes générations ; renforcer l'encadrement parental et améliorer la collaboration entre parents et enseignants. Au cours des assises, les différents acteurs vont participer aux séances plénières, aux communication thématiques, aux discussions générales. D’autres activités attendues seront la restitution des travaux et l’adoption des recommandations assorties d'une feuille de route opérationnelle. Un mécanisme sera mis en place pour le suivi-évaluation de la mise en œuvre des recommandations. Cet article Cameroun : le Nyong et So’o tient des assises stratégiques pour polir l’environnement éducatif est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Port Autonome de Douala : vers une refonte tarifaire sans hausse
data.description: © DR Réunie le 28 août 2026 au siège de l’APN sous la présidence de Serge Patrick Essomba, la 37e session du Comité d’homologation a examiné la demande du PAD visant l’actualisation de son régime tarifaire en vigueur depuis 2022, sans aucune augmentation. Le Port Autonome de Douala révise ses tarifs, mais sans alourdir la facture. La 37e session du Comité Technique d’Homologation des Tarifs des Services Portuaires s’est tenue le 28 août 2026 au siège de l’Autorité Portuaire Nationale (APN), sous la présidence de M. Essomba Serge Patrick, Directeur de la Régulation, de la Compétitivité et des Activités Portuaires. Au cœur des travaux, le projet soumis par le Port Autonome de Douala (PAD). data.title: Université de Dschang : une thèse primée révèle 60% des Camerounais exclus des messages de santé
data.description: © DR À 27 ans, le Dr Ambelem Tangyie Aya-Nwi remporte le prix de la meilleure thèse de la Dschang School of Arts and Social Sciences. Soutenue le 20 mars 2026, sa recherche démontre que l’exclusion linguistique prive 60% des Camerounais des messages de santé et propose de remodeler la communication publique. Et si le plus grand obstacle à la santé n’était pas médical mais linguistique ? C’est la thèse défendue par le Dr Ambelem Tangyie Aya-Nwi, sacré meilleure thèse de Doctorat 2025-2026 de la Dschang School of Arts and Social Sciences (DSASS). Intitulée "A Sociolinguistic Analysis of Social Communication and Social Conflict within the Health Domain in the Multilingual Context of Cameroon", réalisée sous la direction du Pr Emmanuel Nforbi, la recherche s’appuie sur 4 ans d’enquête à Dschang, Bamenda et Douala, avec 500 questionnaires et 100 entretiens, notamment pendant la crise anglophone et la Covid-19. Le constat est politique : le système de santé camerounais prend insuffisamment en compte les réalités culturelles et linguistiques. L’identité culturelle détermine la confiance et l’accès aux soins. Pire, la famille et les amis restent la principale source d’information sanitaire, devant les professionnels. Les messages uniquement en français ou en anglais excluent 60% de la population, surtout rurale. Le jeune chercheur, né en 1999 à Bafoussam et passé par Bafut et l’Université de Bamenda, propose trois ruptures : placer la résolution des conflits au cœur des messages de santé via une approche décentralisée, substituer au message national uniforme des approches identitaires délocalisées, et intégrer réellement la médecine traditionnelle africaine dans la recherche et les soins. Une thèse qui devrait aiguiller les politiques publiques. Cet article Université de Dschang : une thèse primée révèle 60% des Camerounais exclus des messages de santé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Le chanteur et pasteur Carlyto Lassa est décédé à 65 ans aux États-Unis
data.description: Le chanteur et pasteur congolais Carlyto Lassa est décédé lundi 31 août 2026 aux États-Unis, à l’âge de 65 ans. L’annonce a été faite par le chanteur Aimé Nkanu sur sa page Facebook, rapporte l’Agence congolaise de presse (ACP). « C’est avec une profonde douleur et une grande consternation que nous confirmons le décès de notre ami et frère, le Pasteur Carlytho LASSA », a écrit Aimé Nkanu, saluant la mémoire d’un « homme de foi, un serviteur de Dieu » dont la carrière et le ministère ont marqué de nombreuses personnes.

data.title: Cerimedo: cuando MAGA se vuelve local

Los datos revelan la escala, la velocidad y la localización con que un repertorio político transnacional puede volverse doméstico. El trabajo aporta una traducción del concepto de “absolutismo cultural” al terreno concreto de la comunicación política digital y de las redes transnacionales de la nueva derecha. The post Cerimedo: cuando MAGA se vuelve local first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Dan Driscoll renuncia como secretario del Ejército de Estados Unidos
data.description: El secretario del Ejército, Dan Driscoll, dejará su cargo después de 18 meses en el puesto, informó hoy la Casa Blanca. No se dio ninguna razón para la salida de Driscoll, quien es amigo del vicepresidente JD Vance, pero se han reportado las tensiones con el secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth. Es el episodio más reciente de una serie de cambios en la cúpula militar. The post Dan Driscoll renuncia como secretario del Ejército de Estados Unidos first appeared on Cubadebate .
